paras: The lynching of Henderson Fox took place at Trenton, Gibson County, Tennessee, in mid-August 1890, when a mob reported as about 200 men took Fox, a Black prisoner, from the county jail and hanged him. Fox was accused of raping a white girl, Annie Dowling, the previous May, and had been brought back from the Indian Territory days before. White papers in Tennessee and beyond carried the news, most of them stating the accusation as fact.

Fox was accused of assaulting Annie Dowling in Gibson County in May 1890; the Camden Chronicle and the Fort Worth Gazette described her as a twelve-year-old white girl, and the Fort Worth paper added that she was blind. A reward of $150 was offered for his capture.

Early in August, Heck Thomas arrested Fox in the Indian Territory and brought him to Fort Worth, Texas, for safekeeping. On 12 August the Fort Worth Gazette reported that a Tennessee sheriff, whom it placed in "Ray county," had left the city that morning with Fox to take him back to answer the charge.

Fox was then held in the jail at Trenton. According to a Nashville dispatch, the sheriff and jailer tried to keep a mob from the prisoner and summoned a large guard, which surrounded the jail. A mob of about 200 men from the neighborhood where the alleged crime took place ran over the guard and demanded the keys, and the jailer "was compelled to give them up." The men took Fox out and hanged him.
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official inquiry into the lynching appears in the coverage, and no members of the mob were named.

Coverage came entirely from white papers, and no Black-press report of the lynching was found. The Nashville wire ran in the Omaha Daily Bee on 18 August under the headline "Swift Justice to a Black Brute," and it called Fox "the negro who outraged Miss Annie Dowling." The Fort Worth Gazette had already headed its arrest notice "A Brute in Human Shape" and called the charge "a most heinous one."

Tennessee papers gave the lynching a few lines: the Clarksville Daily Tobacco Leaf-Chronicle on 18 August, the Savannah Courier on 21 August and the Camden Chronicle on 22 August. All three stated the rape as fact, and the Camden paper called Fox "a negro fiend." Under the heading "Two Mobs," the Savannah Courier paired the lynching with the hanging and shooting of Tom Woodard, taken from the Humboldt jail by four men.

Weekly news summaries carried the story further, with the Diamond Drill of Crystal Falls, Michigan, printing the name as "Henderson Fax" and calling Dowling "a beautiful young white girl." As late as 4 September, the Lewiston Teller in Idaho listed Fox as "a negro ravisher" lynched at Trenton.

The reports disagree on when the lynching took place: the Nashville wire, dated Sunday 17 August, said Fox was lynched "tonight," while the three Tennessee papers said Saturday night, which fell on 16 August. The Tennessee reports, which were closer to the event and agree with one another, point to Saturday night. The wire said Fox was hanged "to a tree," while the Savannah Courier placed the hanging "in the court house yard at Trenton."

accounts.label: Nashville wire
accounts.gist: Dated 17 August and saying Fox was lynched 'tonight': a mob of about 200 from the neighborhood of the alleged crime overran a guard summoned by the sheriff and jailer, forced the keys from the jailer and hanged Fox to a tree.

accounts.label: Tennessee papers
accounts.gist: Fox was taken from the Trenton jail on Saturday night by a mob of 200 and hanged; the Savannah Courier placed the hanging in the court house yard.

accounts.label: Fort Worth report
accounts.gist: Before the lynching, Fox was arrested in the Indian Territory and taken back to Tennessee by a sheriff to answer a charge of raping a twelve-year-old blind white girl.

framing.detail: The Omaha Bee headed the wire 'Swift Justice to a Black Brute' and stated the outrage as fact.
The Fort Worth Gazette headed its arrest item 'A Brute in Human Shape' and called the alleged crime 'a most heinous one'.
Tennessee briefs reported the lynching flatly but stated the rape as fact; the Camden Chronicle called Fox 'a negro fiend'.
A Michigan weekly news summary called the girl 'a beautiful young white girl'; an Idaho summary reprinted the item calling Fox 'a negro ravisher'.
